newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi forum to discuss $2-3.5 billion projects.
newsitem.headline: Saudi forum to discuss $2-3.5 billion projects.

text.p: A senior Saudi official said on Tuesday an forum on gas usage in the country's industrial cities of Yanbu and Jubail next month would discuss projects worth up to $3.5 billion.

"The...forum on the future use of gas in industry and energy will discuss the possibility of expanding the energy facilities in Yanbu and Jubail at a cost of between $2-3.5 billion," Saudi television quoted Prince Abdullah bin Faisal bin Turki al-Saud, head of the Royal Commission for Jubail and Yanbu as saying.
The state-run television said the forum, which would be held in Yanbu in September, would be attended by the prince and executives from around the world.
The television did not say whether investments would come from the private or public sector.
But the prince had said last year that plans were underway to set up the first utility company in Saudi Arabia with private and foreign participation.

The Royal Commission is setting up The Utility Co with private partners to provide some $500 million equity and raise finance mainly for the expansion of power and water utilities in the two industrial cities where power demand is close to capacity.

The new firm aims to raise billions of dollars to upgrade these facilities to meet industrial demand in the Red Sea and Gulf port cities, which are home to 140 industries accoundting for $30 billion in investment and half Saudi industrial output.
